products.title: Products (RHP)
products.body:
- DRHP: 'Our Company offers a different variety of 14 kits which are majorly used by the police departments, apart from this the company also assembles the kits as per the needs of the clients as well.' Kits are procured from global leaders and assembled at the registered office. Segment stated to contribute 'approx. 30-40% of total revenue from operations'.
- DRHP: 'Till now, our company provide 6 (Six) Handheld devices'. R&D team of 5 members converted promoter's ideas into designs/prototypes; software development outsourced to third parties under NDAs; hardware integration/assembly either outsourced or in-house. DRHP: 'At present, we are not engaged in full manufacturing of these devices; assembling is done in-house or through vendors.' Serial Nos. 1 to 4 are commercialised; 5 and 6 are at demonstration / customer evaluation stage and 'commercial sales have not yet commenced'. Note: the Business Strategies section names the two uncommercialised devices as 'Kwick Smart Handheld 8D Device' and 'Kwick Smart Handheld 4D Device', whereas the product portfolio section names the second 'Kwick Fingerprint 4D'.
- DRHP: 'Our R&D team has developed and designed the prototype model of multiple fuming chambers but as apart of strategic decision, company has outsourced the manufacturing and assembling of these chambers and cabinets.'
- DRHP: 'Although, as of now, Company has sold Mini Mobile CSI Vehicle (SUV, small van) and Macro Mobile CSI Laboratory (large van/traveller bus).' From mid-FY25 the Company shifted to supplying only the digital and scientific kits and outsourcing vehicle procurement and fabrication to local dealers, while its operations team supervises fabrication, electrical/IT integration and kit installation.
- Products supplied standalone or bundled.
- DRHP: 'The Company is an authorised non-exclusive reseller of SmallPond' in India, covering licensing, installation, user training and support.
- DRHP: services portfolio 'includes rental of the Company's purchased products from OEM's as well as sub-leasing of OEM's products, which are first taken on lease from OEM's and then sub-leased to clients with authorization under the governing agreement.'
- DRHP: 'These software platforms are currently under development and their features, deployment timelines, customer acceptance and commercialisation may be subject to technical development, testing, regulatory requirements and tender-specific requirements.' Development began from the start of FY 2025-26. The DRHP states E-Forensics 'comprises of 10 apps' but names only three.
- DRHP: development of the simulator received 'substantial support and, funding from the Ministry of Science & Technology, the Directorate of Forensic Science, and TIFAC'. From FY2015 the Company expanded into fingerprint science and the wider forensic portfolio.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: The Company describes itself as a non-manufacturing procurement, assembly and integration business rather than a vertically integrated manufacturer. Our Business, 'PLANT & MACHINERY, EQUIPMENTS': 'Since, we are not a manufacturing unit, we are mainly engaged in the supplying of Forensic products and assembling of different equipment's and Kits.' BACKWARD LINKAGE: forensic systems and evidence-collection tools are procured through a combination of imports and domestic sourcing. Imports began with Sirchie (USA), from whom the Company 'has obtained representation Certificate ... in India to solicit orders for Sirchie Fingerprint Laboratories'; current OEM engagement is via 'Non-Exclusive distributorship agreement with renowned international OEMs or deal in Purchase order basis', with named OEMs Sirchie (USA), Thermo Fisher Scientific, Invitrogen, Rapiscan Systems, Smallpond, MHC Hardware Software Trading LLC and Seratec. Source countries are stated as 'China, USA, Turkey, Japan, Italy etc.' Import substitution is quantified: the Company 'sourced approximately 65.42%, 85.72% and 91.35% of its raw material requirements locally in the financial years ended March 31, 2024, 2025 and 2026 respectively'; the corresponding procurement table prints Forensic Products & Kits Imported of Rs. 501.39 lakhs / 34.58% (FY24), Rs. 629.01 lakhs / 14.28% (FY25) and Rs. 6,43.82 lakhs [printed thus] / 8.65% (FY26), against domestic purchases of Rs. 948.41 lakhs / 65.42%, Rs. 3,774.42 lakhs / 85.72% and Rs. 6,802.24 lakhs / 91.35%, on total purchases of Rs. 1,449.80 / 4,403.43 / 7,446.06 lakhs. Purchases of Goods represented 85.01%, 81.75% and 54.76% of total expenditure and 70.44%, 67.72% and 48.03% of revenue from operations in FY26, FY25 and FY24 respectively (total expenditure Rs. 8,758.90 / 5,386.43 / 2,647.56 lakhs). LIMITED FORWARD/IN-HOUSE INTEGRATION: kits are assembled in-house at the registered office; handheld-device software development is 'outsourced to third parties under non-disclosure agreements (NDAs)' and hardware integration/assembly is 'either outsourcing ... or do in-house'; fuming chamber and cabinet manufacturing and assembling is outsourced; and from mid-FY25 the Mobile CSI Vehicle model shifted to 'supplying only the digital and scientific kits and outsourcing the vehicle procurement and fabrication work to the local dealers', which the Company states 'reduces capital intensity and working-capital blockage'. Both software prototypes initiated in FY26 (AI-Powered Judicial Assistance Platform, LIMS) were likewise developed 'by outsourcing the development work to a third party, based on the concept and framework developed by the R&D team of Kwick'. LOGISTICS: a dual model - direct delivery from import custom house to customer location for high-value/time-sensitive imported equipment, and central dispatch from the Company's office-cum-warehouse for stocked and pre-assembled kits - executed through third-party (3PL) certified logistics providers. NIL DISCLOSURE: 'We have not entered into any technical or other collaboration as on date.'

demand_drivers.title: Seasonality (RHP report)
demand_drivers.body: AFFIRMATIVE DISCLOSURE - not seasonal. MD&A, item 8: 'Our Company's business is not seasonal. However, the business of the Company does depend on country's economy situation and inflation.' The DRHP does, however, identify tender-cycle timing as a driver of period-to-period variation: 'Tender/award timing and order-book conversion' and 'Customer concentration: Share of revenue from a few large departments/states and timing of their procurement' are both listed under 'FACTORS AFFECTING OUR RESULTS OF OPERATIONS', and Business Strategy 5 states that 'revenue contribution from individual states may vary from year to year depending on tender cycles, order execution and customer procurement timelines'.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- We do not have long-term agreements with a majority of our customers.
- We do not have firm, long-term supply agreements with most customers and primarily rely on purchase orders rather than fixed-term contracts.
- As a result, our customers may amend, reschedule, reduce, or cancel purchase orders prior to finalisation.
- Such changes could disrupt our production planning, lead to sub-optimal capacity utilisation, and adversely affect our revenues, margins, working capital and cash flows.
- Some customer purchase orders include provisions for remedies such as liquidated damages or specific performance in the event of delay or default.
- The loss of this significant or key customer or a reduction in the amount of business could have an adverse effect on our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.
- A reduction in these segments may result from factors such as changes in government procurement policies, budget allocations, adoption of new technologies, increased competition, or shifts in customer preferences.
- We are dependent on a limited number of suppliers for procurement of our raw materials, and the loss of any one or more of our major suppliers would have a material adverse effect on our business operations and profitability.
